# Connections Optimizer

Curated by Skill Harbor: a network-hygiene skill for X and LinkedIn that treats your social graph as something to reorganize, not a one-way prospecting list. You give it your current priorities, target roles or industries, platform selection, a do-not-touch list, and a mode (light-pass, default, or aggressive). It then scores your following and connections on positive signals (reciprocity, recent activity, alignment to priorities, bridge value, real engagement history) and negative ones (abandoned accounts, stale one-way follows, off-priority clusters, repeated non-response), and returns a review pack: prune queue with reasons and confidence, keep and protect list with bridge values, ranked add and follow targets with warm paths, plus draft DMs, LinkedIn messages, or Apple Mail intros. The safety defaults are the point: review-first always, never blind auto-pruning, X prunes only accounts you follow (never followers), LinkedIn 1st-degree removals default to manual review, and it never auto-sends anything. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: it needs real access to your graph to be useful (X API or browser control, LinkedIn API or browser workflow); without that it can only reason from lists you paste in. It pairs with lead-intelligence (lot 50) for target discovery and brand-voice (lot 50) so drafts sound like you. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
